statements: However, it has been surprisingly difficult to train networks to effectively use both modalities in a way that demonstrates gain over single-modality networks.

Our experimental evaluation on the challenging KITTI object detection benchmark, including 3D and bird’s eye view metrics, shows significant improvements, especially at long distance, over the state-of-the-art fusion based methods.

Compared to 2D object detection, which has been well-studied [1], [2], [3], [4], 3D object detection is more challenging with more output parameters needed to specify 3D oriented bounding boxes around targets.

solution.summary: In this paper, we propose a novel Camera-LiDAR Object Candidates (CLOCs) fusion network. We propose Camera-LiDAR Object Candidates Fusion (CLOCs) as a way to achieve improved accuracy for 3D object detection.
solution.approach: In this paper, we propose a novel Camera-LiDAR Object Candidates (CLOCs) fusion network.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we propose a novel Camera-LiDAR Object Candidates (CLOCs) fusion network.
We propose Camera-LiDAR Object Candidates Fusion (CLOCs) as a way to achieve improved accuracy for 3D object detection.
Then, we introduce the motivation of our work and why we choose to fuse the detection candidates in section 3.

evidence.quote: Our experimental evaluation on the challenging KITTI object detection benchmark, including 3D and bird’s eye view metrics, shows significant improvements, especially at long distance, over the state-of-the-art fusion based methods.
This is illustrated in the official KITTI 3D object detection benchmark leaderboard, where LiDAR-only based methods outperform most of the fusion based methods.

limitations.summary: While early and deep fusion have greatest potential to leverage cross modality information, they suffer from sensitivity to data alignment, often involve complicated architectures [11], [12], [13], [14], and typically require pixel-level correspondences of sensor data.
items: While early and deep fusion have greatest potential to leverage cross modality information, they suffer from sensitivity to data alignment, often involve complicated architectures [11], [12], [13], [14], and typically require pixel-level correspondences of sensor data.
However, object detection performance at longer distance is still relatively poor.
However, it is still 2∼4% worse in moderate level than the best LiDARonly based detectors in KITTI leaderboard.
Hence, the multi-modal data does not need to be synchronized or aligned with other modalities.

applications.detail: INTRODUCTION Autonomous driving systems need accurate 3D perception of vehicles and other objects in their environment.

applications.detail: Unlike 2D visual detection, 3D-based object detection enables spatial path planning for object avoidance and navigation.
applications.quote: Unlike 2D visual detection, 3D-based object detection enables spatial path planning for object avoidance and navigation.

applications.detail: Frustum PointNet [24], Pointfusion [13] and Frustum ConvNet [25] are the representatives of 2D driven 3D detectors, which exploit mature 2D detectors to generate 2D proposals and narrow down the 3D processing domain to the corresponding cropped region in the image.
